name: options-boulders-b
prompt: Output ONE image, 16:9. A contact sheet of FOUR separate paintings in a 2 by 2 grid, each the same size, separated by thin plain dark gutters; no labels, no letters, no numbers, no text anywhere. Each painting is a different concept for the same view: the inside of one terrarium room, edge to edge (no case, no frame, no box edges), seen straight on from a low eye height, wide, the back softly out of focus and the ground sharp. Each is a small SHRINE GARDEN, composed like a fine nature aquarium: a CONVEX composition, one mossy island rising in the middle-right carrying ONE small tree and one large mossy hero stone at about 62 percent of the width, the strongest point of the picture; smaller mossy stones of the same kind beside it, odd in number, leaning slightly; a small still dark koi pond set BACK at the foot of the island behind the ground, with a mossy stone rim, no fish painted; the planting rising in levels from the front to the back: low moss at the front, ferns and low shrubs in the middle, the tree and soft foliage at the back. THE GROUND: a living, CALM moss ground in large soft patches with a little fine soil, low in contrast, nothing scattered on it, so small dark, brown and teal creatures read clearly; NO raked sand, NO gravel. One RAISED MOSS TERRACE at the left, a low level about a tenth of the picture higher than the main ground, with a rounded front lip, joined to the main ground by a gentle mossy ramp; its top flat enough to walk on. Two small low foreground pieces at the very front, one in the left third and one in the right third. NO fittings at all: no lantern, no bamboo, no pipes, no gates, no torii, no bridge, no shrine building, no rope. Painted in a warm hand-crafted miniature-diorama finish: fine painterly grain, soft bokeh behind; never photographic, never toon, never childish, no cartoon outlines, no toy colours, no gloss, no glow. No creatures, no animals, no fish, no figures. The four concepts must be clearly different in palette, season, mood and light. TOP LEFT: early summer, a small Japanese maple in fresh green over silver-grey stones, soft green dappled light. TOP RIGHT: autumn, the maple turned warm amber and gold (never bright red), a few gold leaves resting on the moss at the island's foot only, low warm side light. BOTTOM LEFT: a misty morning under a small cedar, cool silver-green moss, pale haze between the levels, soft diffuse light. BOTTOM RIGHT: late afternoon under a small gingko in pale yellow, long warm light and blue shadows across the moss, dark stones with lichen.
